claims.text: REGISTRY CORRESPONDENCE VERIFIED, and it needed no build. ARM-08's code-side registry in RxCounterAuthority.cpp and the §4.1 document registry agree on all six counters: identical membership, identical write-scope (only boss_release_delay true), and identical sim cites. The E11 repair and the C++ gate are the same registry expressed twice.

This is the seam a divergence would hide in: ARM-08 verifies their code, I verify the document, and until now nobody verified the CORRESPONDENCE. A gate that encoded five counters, or marked a second one writable, would pass ARM-08's own tests and pass my document gate simultaneously while contradicting the specification it implements.

Independent corroboration of CHECKPOINT-12. ARM-08's registry cites RxBossEarthquake.h:80 for boss_tremor_stage and carries the comment ':80, not :81. The cite was off by one and line 81 is blank — the pointer tying this counter to a real field resolved to nothing, and nothing noticed, because the gate keys on the counter_id string and never reads the cite.' A different seat reached the same defect by a different route, and their code now matches my corrected document.

tests.command: extract FCounterEntry Registry[] from RxCounterAuthority.cpp; parse §4.1 by header name; compare membership, write-scope and cites

decisions_requested: This closes the part of K-01C that can be done without a build: the code registry provably encodes the specified registry. What remains is BEHAVIOURAL — that AdmitCounterWrite actually refuses boss_stability and admits boss_release_delay at runtime — and that still needs a built editor with ARM-08's code present.
risks: This verifies the TABLE, not the GATE. A correct registry wired to a function that ignores it, or consulted on the wrong code path, would pass this check completely. Correspondence of data is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.

I parsed ARM-08's registry with a regex over their source. If they later express the same registry in a form my pattern does not match, this check silently finds 0 counters and would need its own positive control — the same failure mode as the ripgrep count I got wrong in the M2 replay. Today it found 6 of 6, which is that control.
